plan: Given my private value of $22, I should bid slightly below this value to maximize profit while minimizing the risk of overpaying. A rational strategy would be to bid slightly below my value to avoid paying more than the prize is worth to me. Since all bidders are rational, they will also bid below their values. I will bid $21.9 to maximize my chance of winning without exceeding my value.

To maximize profit, bid slightly above the expected value of the second-highest bid. With values uniformly distributed between $0 and $49, the average is $24.5. Given my value of $34, a bid slightly above $24.5, say $25, balances winning without overpaying. This strategy assumes rational bidders bid near their values.

Given my private value of $10 and the rationality of all bidders, I should bid slightly below my value to maximize potential profit. Bidding exactly $10 risks breaking even or losing if I pay more than the prize's value. A bid of $9.9 allows room to win if competitors bid less than my value while minimizing loss if I overpay slightly.
